name.text: EOT_Q41: Christian Religious Studies JSS1 Assessment

questiontext.text: Which of the following realms or entities were formed during the first three days of creation (the Forming Phase)? (Select all that apply)

generalfeedback.text: Days 1 to 3 formed the cosmic habitats: Day 1 (light/darkness), Day 2 (sky/waters), Day 3 (dry land/seas and vegetation). Birds and marine life were created on Day 5.

name.text: EOT_Q42: Christian Religious Studies JSS1 Assessment

questiontext.text: Which of the following truths represent foundational biblical purposes for marriage instituted by God in Eden? (Select all that apply)

generalfeedback.text: God instituted marriage for companionship (Genesis 2:18), procreation (Genesis 1:28), and mutual complementary support (Genesis 2:24). Treating spouses as commercial chattel violates divine design.

name.text: EOT_Q43: Christian Religious Studies JSS1 Assessment

questiontext.text: Which of the following consequences directly resulted from the disobedience of Adam and Eve in Genesis chapter 3? (Select all that apply)

generalfeedback.text: The Fall resulted in spiritual alienation, guilt, sorrow in childbearing, painful agricultural toil, physical death, and expulsion from Eden (Genesis 3:16-19, 23). The celestial bodies were not destroyed.

name.text: EOT_Q44: Christian Religious Studies JSS1 Assessment

questiontext.text: Which of the following details accurately describe Noah's Ark as specified in Genesis chapter 6? (Select all that apply)

generalfeedback.text: God commanded Noah to make an Ark of gopher wood, coat it with waterproof pitch, and build it with three internal decks (Genesis 6:14-16). Steam engines did not exist.

name.text: EOT_Q45: Christian Religious Studies JSS1 Assessment

questiontext.text: Which of the following moral virtues did Noah exemplify that made him stand out among the people of his generation? (Select all that apply)

generalfeedback.text: Noah was renowned for his righteousness, blameless walk with God, unwavering faith, and exact obedience to divine commands (Genesis 6:9, 22; Hebrews 11:7).

name.text: EOT_Q46: Christian Religious Studies JSS1 Assessment

questiontext.text: Match each day of the creation week with the specific creation work accomplished on that day:

generalfeedback.text: Day 1 brought light; Day 2 established the sky/firmament; Day 4 placed the celestial lights; and Day 6 created terrestrial animals and mankind.

name.text: EOT_Q47: Christian Religious Studies JSS1 Assessment

questiontext.text: Match each biblical figure or entity from Genesis 1–3 with their specific role or characteristic:

generalfeedback.text: Adam was fashioned from dust; Eve was formed from his rib; the serpent was the crafty deceiver; and cherubim guarded the way to the tree of life.

name.text: EOT_Q48: Christian Religious Studies JSS1 Assessment

questiontext.text: Match each consequence of the Fall with the recipient on whom it was pronounced:

generalfeedback.text: Genesis 3 assigns specific judgments: the serpent crawls on its belly; the woman experiences sorrow in childbearing; the man toils with sweat; and the ground yields thorns and thistles.

name.text: EOT_Q49: Christian Religious Studies JSS1 Assessment

questiontext.text: Match each item from the account of the Great Flood with its biblical significance:

generalfeedback.text: Gopher wood built the Ark; pitch sealed it from water; Mount Ararat received the resting Ark; and the plucked olive leaf proved land vegetation had sprouted.

name.text: EOT_Q50: Christian Religious Studies JSS1 Assessment

questiontext.text: Match each biblical covenant or theological concept with its core scriptural definition:

generalfeedback.text: Creatio Ex Nihilo is creation from nothing; Imago Dei is the image of God in humans; Protoevangelium is the promise of redemption; and the rainbow is the perpetual sign of the Noahic covenant.
